title: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain
publication: RescueSpeech: A German Corpus for Speech Recognition in Search and Rescue Domain (Sagar et al.; arXiv:2306.04054)
production_type: primary spontaneous/task speech from simulated search-and-rescue exercises; clean speech plus synthetic noisy derivatives
manual_evidence: Zenodo v2 explicitly states that the authentic native-German recordings are manually annotated
available_primary_data: Readme.md; Task_ASR.tar.gz (clean primary recordings plus annotations/splits and synthetic noisy counterparts); Task_enhancement.tar.gz (derived noisy speech-enhancement material)
notes: Core eligibility is restricted to the authentic manually annotated clean recordings and their human annotations. Synthetic noisy copies and third-party AudioSet noise are lineage/derived artifacts and must not be counted as independent production. Zenodo reports 2412 ASR recordings, 1:36:10, 26 speakers, 38 recordings with undetermined speaker. Preserve source inconsistency: README split totals 1591+576+245=2412 but printed Totals row incorrectly says 2167.
